environment: Vercel Sandbox, 2 vCPUs / 4 GiB, nested restricted Docker, live IBM Bob Shell, Chromium

analysis.summary: Zero-dependency Node.js ESM project. No build step or package install is required — there are no npm dependencies. The server is started with `node app.mjs` and listens on PORT (default 3100). Unit tests use Node's built-in test runner (`node --test`) and cover ordinary orders, free-shipping orders, and invalid inputs. A known boundary defect exists: the free-shipping threshold in shipping.mjs uses `subtotal > 100` instead of `subtotal >= 100`, so an order of exactly $100 incorrectly incurs a $5 charge.
analysis.purpose: Shipping Service is a small checkout web application that helps online shoppers see their delivery cost before they pay. A shopper enters their order subtotal on the webpage and the app instantly shows the shipping charge and final total. Orders under $100 pay a flat $5 shipping fee; orders of $100 or more ship free. There is no payment processing or external service — it is a self-contained quote tool.
capabilities: View a checkout form in the browser to enter an order subtotal
Receive an instant shipping cost and order total for a valid subtotal
Get a clear error message when an invalid subtotal (zero, negative, non-numeric, or over $10,000) is submitted
Query the quote API directly via GET /quote?subtotal=<amount> for programmatic use
Receive a 404 response for any unrecognised route

languages.name: JavaScript
languages.role: Implements the entire server (HTTP routing, request handling) and the shipping-quote business logic, plus the in-browser form interaction and the checked-in unit tests

languages.name: HTML
languages.role: Defines the static checkout form page served at GET /

stack: Node.js 22+ (ESM, built-in http, fs/promises, test runner)
limitations: The project contains a documented deliberate defect: subtotal === 100 returns shipping:5 instead of shipping:0 because the threshold condition is `subtotal > 100` rather than `subtotal >= 100`.
There are no lint, type-check, or coverage scripts in package.json; the checks array contains only the existing test runner invocation.
index.html has no dedicated test; its correctness can only be verified via an end-to-end browser or HTTP test outside the checked-in suite.
No CI configuration file (e.g. .github/workflows) was present in the snapshot, so the runtime version is inferred solely from the engines field in package.json.
assumptions: No npm install step is needed because package.json declares no dependencies; the project runs on Node.js stdlib alone.
The server binds to 127.0.0.1 (loopback); test workers are assumed to share the application network namespace so this does not block HTTP-level checks.
The engines field specifies node>=22; node:22-bookworm is selected as the closest available pinned image.

issues.title: Free-shipping threshold boundary
issues.description: The free-shipping threshold in shipping.mjs uses a strict greater-than comparison (`subtotal > 100`) instead of greater-than-or-equal (`subtotal >= 100`). As a result, an order of exactly $100 is charged $5 shipping, contradicting the documented contract: "Orders of $100 or more receive free shipping, including exactly $100."

reproduction.action: GET /quote?subtotal=100 (exact threshold — expects free shipping per docs)

issues.expected: subtotal=100 returns shipping:0 (documented); subtotal=100.01 returns shipping:0; subtotal=101 returns shipping:0

actual.label: GET /quote?subtotal=100 (exact threshold — expects free shipping per docs)

issues.rootCause: In `shipping.mjs` line 5, the expression `subtotal > 100 ? 0 : 5` excludes the boundary value 100 from free shipping. The correct operator is `>=`. The README, the HTML copy, and the issue contract all specify that $100 qualifies for free shipping.
issues.recommendedFix: Change `subtotal > 100` to `subtotal >= 100` on line 5 of shipping.mjs.
issues.fixExplanation: Replacing `>` with `>=` makes the boundary inclusive. With this change: subtotal=100 → shipping:0, total:100 (matches docs); subtotal=100.01 → shipping:0 (already correct, unchanged); subtotal=99.99 → shipping:5 (still correct). No other logic is affected. The existing passing tests (subtotal=50 → $5, subtotal=150 → $0) continue to pass. A new boundary test for subtotal=100 would also pass.
issues.risks: No adverse risks identified for this single-character operator change. The only behavioral change is at exactly subtotal=100, which is the documented free-shipping boundary. All other input ranges are unaffected. No existing passing tests are broken.

fixes.explanation: Replace the strict `>` comparison with `>=` on the shipping-rate line in shipping.mjs. Every other character in the file is preserved exactly.
fixes.risks: Minimal. Only the exact boundary value 100 changes behavior (from $5 to $0 shipping), which is the intended correction. All other paths are unchanged.

No CI configuration file (e.g. .github/workflows) was present in the snapshot, so the runtime version is inferred solely from the engines field in package.json.

The documented deliberate defect (subtotal===100 charges $5 instead of $0) means http-2 step 'GET /quote?subtotal=100' is expected to FAIL until the defect in shipping.mjs is corrected — the test is intentionally written against documented correct behavior to expose the bug.
There is no authentication, session, or multi-step checkout flow to test beyond the single quote endpoint.

The rounding assertion for subtotal=50.005 (http-5 last step) depends on IEEE 754 floating-point behavior of Number('50.005') + 5; the exact rounded value 55.01 is an assumption based on Math.round((55.005)*100)/100.
No lint, typecheck, or coverage scripts exist; those checks cannot be generated.
index.html has no server-side template logic; browser tests cover its only interactive behavior (form submit → fetch → output rendering).
POST /quote body content-type behavior is untested beyond 404 routing because the server does not parse request bodies.
AI-inferred expectations can be wrong; assumptions are labelled. This is measured coverage, not a guarantee of all defects.
Linux containers do not emulate proprietary hardware, native Windows/macOS UI or unavailable external services.
